title: Buffalo Sabres trade goalie Devon Levi to Edmonton Oilers for a third-round pick
content:
The Buffalo Sabres traded goalie Devon Levi and a 2028 seventh-round pick to the Edmonton Oilers for a 2028 third-round pick.

Levi, 24, spent last season playing exclusively in the AHL and had a .904 save percentage and a 2.83 goals-against average in 52 games for the Rochester Americans. At one point, however, Levi looked like the Sabres’ goalie of the future. In 2021, the Sabres traded Sam Reinhart to the Florida Panthers for Levi and a 2022 first-round pick that became center Jiri Kulich.

When Buffalo signed him after he had one of the most dominant careers in college hockey history, he stepped into the NHL and started seven games with a 2.94 goals-against average and .905 save percentage.

That small sample of strong play at the end of the 2022-23 season caused then-general manager Kevyn Adams to think he was ready to be a full-time NHLer the next season, even though very few goalies in NHL history have made the jump right from college. Levi struggled in 2023-24 with a 3.10 goals-against average and an .899 save percentage in 23 games before getting sent down to the AHL. He thrived that season in Rochester with a 2.42 goals-against average and .927 save percentage.

The next season, the Sabres tried to start him in the NHL again, but he didn’t look ready. He had a 4.12 goals-against average and .872 save percentage before getting sent down to the AHL. That’s where he’s been ever since.

Prior to last season, the Sabres made a few moves that hinted at Levi not being in their plans. They signed Alex Lyon to be Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen’s backup. Then they claimed Colten Ellis on waivers at the end of the preseason. Ellis is just a year older than Levi and ended up spending the entire season in the NHL.

Levi will require waivers beginning this season, so the Sabres needed to make a move with four goalies under contract. Levi, who’s undersized but a strong athlete who thinks the game at a high level, gets a chance at a fresh start on a team that has been looking for an answer in net. Currently, Tristan Jarry and Levi are the only two goalies under contract for the Oilers. Connor Ingram, who started five of Edmonton’s six playoff games, became a free agent on July 1.
